newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Finn buying helps Estonian bourse to record close.
newsitem.headline: Finn buying helps Estonian bourse to record close.

text.p: Estonian shares maintained their rise to set new records on Thursday with strong buying pressure from Helsinki helping drive prices higher by the close, dealers said.
"The Estonian market is ready for a correction, but Helsinki is keeping up the interest in Hansapank and this is affecting Hoiupank and keeping the whole market higher," one dealer said.
"We really don't know how far it can go, but we expect a correction soon," one trader said.
Total trade on the main list was 68.5 million kroons with the Talse index 2.70 percent higher at 310.46.
Hansapank started the bull run off in morning trade and dominated trade during the day. It saw trade worth 27.1 million kroons to close seven kroons up at 175.50 kroons.
"It was interest from Helsinki that was driving the bourse higher, but dealers over there are not sure what is pushing the prices higher," one dealer said.
In Helsinki, Hansa shares were traded higher to close 3.90 markka up at 67 markka on 1.8 million markka trade.
"We don't know how far this will go, but whoever is buying in Helsinki is paying a markka more for shares compared to trading in Estonia," dealer said.
Hoiupank fell in early trade but rebounded to close at 174 kroons, up 5.90 kroons on turnover of 15 million kroons.
On the free market, privatisation securities were the most traded but fell in both price and trade with only 6.5 million kroons traded.
